latest_nl_proof:
Let A and B be finite sets, and suppose there exists an injective function f : A -> B. We must prove |A| <= |B|.

Because A and B are finite, there exist natural numbers n and m such that |A| = n and |B| = m. We will show n <= m.

Consider the image f(A) = {f(a) : a in A} subseteq B. Since f is injective, the map f regarded as a function from A onto f(A) is bijective: it is surjective onto f(A) by definition of image, and it is injective by hypothesis. Therefore A and f(A) have the same cardinality, so
|A| = |f(A)|.

Now f(A) is a subset of B. Since B is finite, every subset of B has cardinality at most that of B. Hence
|f(A)| <= |B|.

Combining the two equalities/inequalities gives
|A| = |f(A)| <= |B|,
so |A| <= |B|, as required.

This proves that for all finite sets A and B, if there exists an injective function f : A -> B, then |A| <= |B|.
role_in_parent: Converts the injective map on finite Kunz sets into the desired inequality of their cardinalities.
statement_nl: Let A and B be finite sets. If there exists an injective function f from A to B, then the cardinality of A is less than or equal to the cardinality of B.

domain_restrictions: f is a function with domain exactly A and codomain exactly B (f: A → B)
injectivity means: for all a1, a2 in A, if a1 ≠ a2 then f(a1) ≠ f(a2)
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For all finite sets A and B, if there exists an injective function f: A → B, then |A| ≤ |B|.
quantifier_order: Let A be a finite set
Let B be a finite set
If there exists a function f: A → B such that f is injective, then |A| ≤ |B|

variables.name: A
variables.role: source set for injection; domain of f

variables.name: B
variables.role: target set for injection; codomain of f

variables.domain: set of all functions A → B
variables.name: f
variables.role: witness of injectivity from A into B

witness_dependencies: The existence witness f depends on the particular sets A and B under consideration (f is not fixed across different A, B).
